title: Agavotaguerra language - Wikipedia
text: Agavotaguerra (Agavotoqueng) is a supposed, extinct Arawakan language of Brazil. Ethnologue leaves it "unclassified", but notes that it is related to Waura and Yawalapiti, which suggests that it is an Arawakan language of the Xingu group. [1]

title: Yawalapití language - Wikipedia
text: The Agavotaguerra (Agavotoqueng) reportedly spoke the same language. [2] Speakers of the language live in a village along the edge of the river Tuatuari, a tributary of the Kuluene River, located in the southern part of the Xingu Indigenous Park (Upper Xingu), in the state of Mato Grosso.
